cli.client.flag.header: extra request header as "Name: Value" or "Name=Value" (repeatable; also VMFLOW_HEADERS, ;-separated)
cli.client.flag.tls_ca_file: CA bundle to verify the daemon management certificate (for private/self-signed CAs)
cli.client.flag.tls_client_cert: client certificate for mTLS (required when the server sets control_tls.client_ca_file)
cli.client.flag.tls_client_key: client key for mTLS (required together with -tls-client-cert)
cli.client.flag.tls_skip_verify: skip server certificate verification (dangerous, debug only)
cli.ctl.usage:
Usage:
  vmflow ctl [flags] <health|rules|stats|metrics|precheck|reload>

Queries a running local vmflow daemon. Response bodies are printed unchanged.

Options:
cli.error.control_port: control-port must be 0 (use config) or between 1 and 65535
cli.mcp.error.credentials: daemon management address must not contain credentials
cli.mcp.error.host: daemon management address requires a host
cli.mcp.error.loopback: daemon management address must use localhost or a loopback IP
cli.mcp.error.path: daemon management address must not contain a path
cli.mcp.error.query: daemon management address must not contain a query or fragment
cli.mcp.error.scheme: daemon management address must use http or https
cli.mcp.error.tls_requires_https: MCP TLS options require an https daemon management address
cli.mcp.usage:
Usage:
  vmflow mcp [flags]

Starts a read-only MCP server over stdio for a running local vmflow daemon.

Options:
cli.service.flag.binary: path to the vmflow binary (default: this executable; install requires a trusted root/admin-owned absolute path)
cli.service.flag.config: config file path the service runs with (default: platform system path)
cli.service.flag.control_port: override the daemon local management port
cli.service.flag.extra_arg: append a future daemon flag as --extra-arg=-flag=value (repeatable; existing flags have dedicated options)
cli.service.flag.log_file: override daemon log destination (Windows default: C:\ProgramData\vmflow\logs\vmflow.log)
cli.service.flag.user: [systemd] run as this user; created if missing (default: root)
cli.service.output.files_preserved: config and log files were left in place; remove them manually if desired
cli.service.output.linux_logs: logs: journalctl -u %s   |   status: vmflow service status
cli.service.output.windows_running: service %s %s and running (start=automatic, restart on failure)
cli.service.usage:
Usage:
  vmflow service (install|start|uninstall|status) [flags]

Registers or starts vmflow as a native service that starts at boot and restarts on crash:
  Linux:   systemd unit (/etc/systemd/system/<name>.service)
  macOS:   launchd daemon (/Library/LaunchDaemons/io.cloudapp.<name>.plist)
  Windows: Windows Service (manage via services.msc)

Options:
cli.tui.service.not_installed: The local vmflow system service is required before opening the TUI, but it is not installed.
cli.tui.service.stopped: The local vmflow system service is required before opening the TUI, but it is stopped.
cli.uninstall.flag.dry_run: print what would be removed without removing it
cli.uninstall.note.service: stop and remove native service (systemd / launchd / Windows Service)
cli.uninstall.output.service_stop_failed: uninstall stopped before removing files because the native service may still be running:
cli.uninstall.plan.nothing: Nothing to remove: vmflow does not appear to be installed.
cli.uninstall.usage:
Usage:
  vmflow uninstall [--dry-run]

Removes the native service, the vmflow binary, and purges config, logs,
vmflow-owned cache artifacts, and the self-update cache. External TLS files are preserved.

Options:
cli.update.error.empty_result: failed to check for updates: empty result
cli.update.error.positionals: update does not accept positional args
cli.update.error.release_unavailable: failed to install update: release metadata is unavailable
cli.update.error.tagged_build: self-update requires a tagged release build; current version is %q (use --version vX.Y.Z to install a specific release)
cli.update.error.windows: self-update is not supported on Windows; install the release ZIP manually
cli.update.flag.version: install or inspect a specific release tag
